headline: BIS CRS registration for electronics & IT products
lead: Mandatory before you manufacture, import or sell any notified electronic product in India. We identify your IS standard, book a BIS-recognised lab, file on Manak Online and deliver your R-number — typically in 4 to 8 weeks.
includes: Product classification and correct IS standard identification
Test coordination with BIS-recognised, NABL-accredited labs
Authorised Indian Representative (AIR) for foreign manufacturers
Complete technical file and Manak Online filing
BIS query handling until the R-number is granted
Renewal tracking so your registration never lapses
overview: The Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) was introduced in 2012 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and is run by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). It ensures that notified electronic and IT goods sold in India meet the applicable Indian Standard for safety.

CRS works on self-declaration of conformity backed by testing at a BIS-recognised laboratory. Unlike the ISI mark, there is no mandatory factory inspection. Once registered, your product carries the BIS Standard Mark with a unique R-number (R-XXXXXXXX).
The scheme has two goals: protect consumers from unsafe and substandard electronics, and give genuine, high-quality products — imported or made in India — straightforward market access.

documents.title: Manufacturer documents
items: Manufacturing licence or business registration certificate
List of machinery and test equipment
Authorisation letter for the authorised signatory

documents.title: Product documents
items: Test report from a BIS-recognised lab (not older than 90 days)
Critical Components List (CCL) or Bill of Materials
Technical specifications, drawings and circuit diagrams
Declaration of Conformity in the prescribed format

documents.title: Foreign manufacturers also need
items: Nomination of an Authorised Indian Representative (AIR)
Power of Attorney from the manufacturer to the AIR

steps.title: Classification & document prep
steps.text: We confirm the product category and exact IS standard, then compile the manufacturer, product and AIR documents.

steps.title: Testing at a BIS-recognised lab
steps.text: Samples are tested against the relevant IS code — e.g. IS 13252 (Part 1) for IT equipment. The test report must be under 90 days old when filed.

steps.title: Online application
steps.text: We file Form I on the Manak Online CRS portal with the test report, Declaration of Conformity and all supporting documents.

steps.title: BIS scrutiny & grant
steps.text: BIS reviews the application. We respond to any queries quickly; on approval you receive the certificate and R-number.

steps.title: Product marking
steps.text: Apply the Standard Mark with your R-number on the product, packaging and manual as per BIS marking guidelines.

consequences.title: Why CRS is mandatory
consequences.text: The Compulsory Registration Order prohibits manufacturing, storing for sale, importing, selling or distributing notified goods without a valid registration.

items.title: Customs rejection
items.text: Shipments without a valid CRS mark are held or denied clearance at the port.

items.title: Seizure & penalties
items.text: Non-compliant stock in the market can be seized, with fines and legal action against the brand.

items.title: Marketplace delisting
items.text: Amazon, Flipkart and other platforms require a valid R-number to list notified products.

tip.title: The #1 cause of CRS delays: the wrong standard
tip.text: A smart TV may need separate registrations for the display and its adaptor. Thresholds like 32" screens or 200 W amplifiers change the requirement. Every engagement starts with a technical review so you are tested once, against the right standard.

costs.title: BIS government fees
costs.text: Application fee, registration fee and renewal fee paid directly to BIS. Fixed and published by BIS.

costs.title: Lab testing fees
costs.text: Varies by product type, complexity and number of models or series. The largest variable cost.

costs.title: Instacertify professional fee
costs.text: Technical review, documentation, lab liaison, filing, query handling and AIR support — quoted as a fixed fee.

validity: Initial registration is granted for 2 years.
Renewal can be filed up to 90 days before expiry, for 2–5 years.
A fresh test report may be needed if the standard has been revised.
A lapsed registration means sales must stop until a new one is granted — we track every deadline for you.

faqs.a: CRS is the Compulsory Registration Scheme run by BIS under MeitY. It requires notified electronic and IT products — mobiles, laptops, chargers, LED lights and more — to be tested in India and registered before they are sold.

faqs.q: How long does CRS registration take?
faqs.a: Usually 4 to 8 weeks from sample submission to grant, depending on lab slot availability, product complexity and how quickly BIS queries are answered.

faqs.q: What does the BIS Standard Mark look like?
faqs.a: For CRS products it is the BIS logo with the registration number (R-XXXXXXXX) printed below it. You can verify any R-number in the BIS Care app.

faqs.q: Who can apply — importer or manufacturer?
faqs.a: Only the manufacturer can hold the registration. Foreign manufacturers must appoint an Authorised Indian Representative (AIR), which we can provide. Importers and traders cannot apply on their own.

faqs.q: Can I import notified products without CRS?
faqs.a: No. Customs will hold or reject commercial shipments of notified products without a valid registration. Limited exemptions exist for R&D samples, which need a separate approval.

faqs.q: Do I need to retest every year?
faqs.a: No. If the design and components stay the same, retesting is not normally required. BIS may still draw market samples, and a revised standard can require a fresh report at renewal.

faqs.q: Does CRS apply to components or spare parts?
faqs.a: CRS applies to finished products in the notified list, not individual components or spares, unless BIS specifically notifies them.

faqs.q: Can one registration cover multiple models?
faqs.a: Yes, models in the same series that share critical components can often be grouped under one registration, which reduces testing cost. We plan the series structure up front.
